Petya has two numbers written next to each other. Determine if they make a lucky pair. We'll say that two numbers make a lucky pair if we can erase exactly one digit in one of these numbers so that the first number becomes equal to the second number.

If it is impossible to erase exactly one digit in one of the numbers so that the first number becomes equal to the second number, print "-1" without the quotes. Otherwise, print any suitable digit.
If all digits in both numbers are equal and erasing any digit won't make them equal again, print "-1".

7

Problem: You have decided to watch the best moments of some movie. There are two buttons on your player:

The movie has n + 2 frames, numbered them from 0 to n + 1. The frame 0 contains the beginning of the movie, the frame n + 1 contains its end.
You will need t seconds to watch the whole movie (i.e. to see all frames from 1 to n). Also you've got a chance to watch some part of the movie before it starts. Let's call this part a prewatched segment. Initially your watching time counter is equal to 0, and the counter of frames watched is also equal to 0.
You don't want to skip interesting frames, but at the same time you don't want to watch the same frame several times. So you have understood that it's better to watch only once every k-th frame of the movie. In other words, there is a list of frames which you simply must have seen. At least once. And all others — you may watch or not, it does not matter.
Therefore, you have defined function f(s), where s is a binary string of length n + 2. Element i of string s is equal to '1', if frame i must be watched, and '0' otherwise. Value f(s) is defined as follows: representation of number f(s) in base-k is correct if and only if exactly one character among characters '1' of string s equals '1'. Otherwise, value of f(s) is 0. Before starting to watch the movie, you may choose any number (not necessary integer') x. When the movie ends, you will have achieved your goal if value x·f(s) is maximum possible.
However, before you go to watch the movie, you wonder whether it is worth watching at all. To do this, you need to know sum S(x) over all possible values of f(s). Here we consider only such strings s, that at least one character of string s is equal to '1'.
